transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in today?

I came in because I’m just… worn out all the time. Not just normal tired, like after a busy week, but this heavy kind of exhaustion. Even if I’m in bed for a full night, I wake up feeling like my body is made of sandbags, and then the whole day feels like I’m dragging myself through wet cement.

Getting through work has been taking everything I have, and even small things at home—like folding laundry or doing basic chores—feel weirdly overwhelming because I’m so tired. It’s frustrating because I feel like I should be able to just push through, but lately it feels like there’s nothing there to push with.
Have you noticed that you’re not getting as much enjoyment out of things you used to like—like hobbies, time with friends, or even simple pleasures like a good meal or a TV show?

Yeah… definitely. That’s actually been one of the stranger parts, because I used to be pretty intentional about making time for things I liked. I’d go hiking when I could, even if it was just a short trail, and I used to do yoga because it made me feel like I was sort of resetting myself. I have a little garden too, and normally I’d be out there fussing over it, checking what was growing, pulling weeds, taking pictures of birds that came around.

But lately I just… don’t. I keep canceling plans to go hiking, or I tell myself I’ll do yoga later and then I never do. My camera has basically been sitting in the closet, and that feels sad because bird photos used to be something I really enjoyed. Now even when I think about doing those things, it doesn’t feel exciting or relaxing. It just feels like more effort, and I can’t seem to convince myself it’s worth it.
Have you been feeling down or depressed most of the day, nearly every day, for at least the last two weeks?

Yes… most days, yeah. It’s not always like crying or some obvious dramatic sadness, but it’s there almost every morning when I wake up. I get this heavy, flat feeling in my chest, like the day is already too much before I’ve even started it.

Sometimes I’ll just sit at the kitchen table with my coffee and stare out at the yard, and it’s like my mind goes to this place where I can’t picture things getting better. Not in a very clear, planned-out way or anything, just this awful feeling like… there isn’t a good version of the future coming. Like everything ahead is just going to be more of the same heaviness.

And it hangs around for so much of the day. I can get distracted for a little while if I have to focus on something, but underneath it, that depressed, weighed-down feeling is still there.
Can you describe how your interest in things has changed lately? Like, do you still find any part of those activities interesting, or has that all faded completely?

It’s faded a lot. I don’t know if I’d say every single tiny bit of interest is gone, because sometimes I’ll still notice something like, “Oh, the weather would be nice for a hike,” or I’ll see a bird out the window and some part of me thinks, “Normally I’d grab the camera for that.” But it doesn’t turn into actually wanting to do it, if that makes sense.

I used to make time for those things. Hiking, yoga, working in the garden, taking bird photos — those were things I cared about and would plan around. Now I keep canceling or putting them off. I’ll tell myself I should go for even a short walk or roll out the yoga mat, and then it feels like this huge task instead of something restorative. The garden is just sitting there needing attention, and I know that would’ve bothered me before.

And my camera’s literally just been in the closet. I’ll think about getting it out, but then it’s like… why? It doesn’t feel worth the effort. Not in the way it used to. It’s like the part of me that got satisfaction from those things has gone really quiet.
Have you been feeling like you’re not good enough, or that you’re failing at things, even when others might not see it that way?

Yeah… I have. A lot, actually. It’s been kind of stuck on this one thing with the mortgage decision. I keep replaying it in my head over and over, like I’m trying to find the exact moment where I should have known better or stopped it or said no.

And the thing is, my husband keeps reminding me that we made that decision together. He’ll say, “This wasn’t just you,” or “We both looked at it, we both agreed,” and logically I can hear that. I can repeat it back. But it doesn’t really land. Emotionally it still feels like I did something selfish and reckless, like I pushed us into something that put the whole household at risk.

I’ll sit there thinking, what kind of person does that? What kind of wife makes a choice that could hurt everyone’s stability? And then I feel ashamed, like I should have been more careful, more responsible, more… I don’t know, adult, I guess. Even if no one else is blaming me the way I’m blaming myself, I still feel like I failed.
Have you noticed any changes in your appetite or weight recently—like eating a lot less or more than usual, or losing or gaining weight without trying?

I’m not really sure, honestly. I haven’t been tracking it closely or anything. I don’t think there’s been some big, obvious change where my clothes suddenly fit differently or people are commenting on it.

My eating has maybe been a little inconsistent just because I’m not paying as much attention to it, but I can’t say I’ve clearly lost or gained weight. Some days I’ll realize I didn’t really think much about food until later, and other days I eat more normally. But nothing stands out to me as a definite appetite or weight change.
Have you noticed any changes in your sleep lately—like trouble falling asleep, waking up a lot during the night, or sleeping much more than usual even though you don’t feel rested?

I’m not totally sure. I haven’t noticed a really clear change that I could point to, like, “Oh, now I’m sleeping all day,” or “I’m awake every night at 3 a.m.” Nothing that definite.

I mean, some nights are better than others, but that’s kind of always been true for me depending on the day and how wound up I am before bed. I haven’t been keeping track of it, so I don’t want to overstate it. I wouldn’t say sleep has stood out to me as the main thing that’s different lately. If there’s been a shift, it’s subtle enough that I’m not really confident saying yes.
Have you noticed yourself moving more slowly than usual, or feeling restless and unable to sit still, especially when you're not trying to be calm or focused?

Yeah… my husband has actually mentioned that. I don’t always notice it in the moment, which is kind of embarrassing, but he’ll say I’m moving around the house like I’m underwater. Like everything I do is slower than it should be—walking from one room to another, picking something up, even just getting myself to start doing whatever I was about to do.

And when he asks me something really simple, like a normal household question, sometimes it takes me a while to answer. It’s not that I didn’t hear him, exactly. It’s more like my brain has to push the words through mud before they come out. I’ll know I need to respond, and I can feel him waiting, but my answer comes out so slowly, or I pause for too long before I can say anything.

I don’t think I’ve been more restless or unable to sit still, at least not that I’m aware of. It’s more the slowed-down thing that he’s pointed out.
Have you noticed a significant loss of energy or have you been feeling fatigued much more easily, even without doing anything physically demanding?

Yes. That’s actually one of the main reasons I came in, because I feel worn out almost all the time, and it’s not like normal “I had a busy day” tired. It feels heavier than that.

Even if I’ve been in bed for a full night, my body still feels like it’s made of sandbags. Getting up and getting through a workday feels like I’m dragging myself from one thing to the next. And even small things at home—like folding laundry or just doing basic chores—can feel like they take everything I have. It’s frustrating because I’ll look at something that should be simple, and it feels like some huge task, not because it’s complicated, but because I just don’t have the energy in me.
Have you had similar periods of feeling this way before, where you experienced these symptoms of low mood, fatigue, and loss of interest?

I’m not really sure how to answer that, honestly. I mean, I’ve had times before where I wasn’t feeling great or where I felt kind of worn down, but I don’t know if it was the same as this, or if I’d be connecting dots that maybe aren’t actually there.

I haven’t really kept a clear mental record of, like, “this happened before and lasted this long and had these exact symptoms.” I tend to just push through things and then later it all kind of blurs together. So I can say I’ve had rough stretches, but whether they were truly similar to what’s been going on now with the low mood and the fatigue and not being interested in things… I don’t feel confident saying yes in a definite way.

I guess my honest answer is: maybe, but I’m not sure. This is standing out to me now more because it’s affecting me enough that I’m talking about it, if that makes sense.

Can you recall if you’ve had at least one other time in your life, before this current period, where you felt down or lost interest in things for at least two weeks and had several other symptoms like fatigue, guilt, or trouble enjoying activities?

I’m sorry, I wish I could give you a cleaner answer, but I really don’t know for sure.

When you put it that specifically—like at least two weeks, feeling down or not interested in things, plus other things going on—I can’t confidently point to a time and say, “Yes, that was definitely it.” I’ve had periods in my life where I felt low or kind of checked out, and I know there have been times where I was tired or harder on myself than usual, but I don’t remember them clearly enough to know if they met what you’re describing.

Part of the problem is that I don’t think I was paying attention to it in that structured of a way. I’d usually just think, “I’m stressed,” or “I’m in a bad stretch,” and keep going. So looking back now, it’s all a little blurry. I can’t honestly say yes, there was definitely another episode like this before. It’s more like… maybe there were times that had pieces of it, but I’m not sure they lasted that long or had enough of the same symptoms.

Can you recall if you’ve ever had a period in the past where you felt down or lost interest in things for at least two weeks and also had several other symptoms like fatigue, guilt, or trouble enjoying activities—even if you didn’t seek help for it at the time?

I hear what you’re asking, and I know you’re trying to pin it down more clearly, but I still don’t think I can honestly say yes.

I can think of times where I wasn’t myself, or where I was kind of going through the motions, but when you ask whether it was at least two weeks and whether there were several other things happening at the same time, I just… I don’t know. I didn’t track it that way, and I don’t want to accidentally turn a vague memory into something more definite than it really was.

There were stretches where I probably would have said I was stressed or burned out, and maybe I wasn’t enjoying things as much, but I can’t clearly remember the length of time or whether it was really the same kind of thing. So my best answer is still that I’m not sure. It’s possible, but I can’t confidently recall a specific past period that fits that description.

Have you ever had a time in your life before this current period where you felt down nearly every day and lost interest in things for at least two weeks, along with other symptoms like fatigue, guilt, or trouble enjoying activities—even if you didn’t talk to anyone about it at the time?

I’m trying to think about it the way you’re asking, and I know you’ve asked it a few different ways, but I still don’t feel like I can give you a solid yes.

The “nearly every day for at least two weeks” part is where I get stuck. I can remember times in the past where I felt pretty low or like I was just not enjoying much, but I don’t know if it was every day, or most days, or if it was more like a few bad days scattered through a stressful period. And with the fatigue or guilt or not enjoying things… I mean, those are things I can imagine being there, but I don’t have a clear memory of them all happening together in a way that I could honestly say matched what you’re describing.

I think at the time I probably would have explained it as being overworked or having a hard time, not as something I was tracking. So looking back now, it’s kind of fuzzy. I don’t want to say “no, never,” because I’m not completely sure that’s true, but I also don’t want to say “yes, definitely,” because I can’t point to a specific period before this one that I remember clearly enough.

So I guess the most accurate answer is: I don’t know. It’s possible there were times that were somewhat like that, but I can’t confidently recall one.

Can you think back to any time before this current period when you had a clear stretch of at least two weeks where you felt down most days and also experienced several other symptoms like fatigue, loss of interest in things, or feelings of guilt—even if you didn’t talk to a doctor about it at the time?

I know you’re asking for a clear stretch, and I’m trying not to be evasive, but I still don’t think I can give you that clearly.

When I look back, I can remember vague periods where I felt low or kind of flat, like I wasn’t really getting much out of things, but I can’t honestly say, “Yes, that was at least two weeks, most days, with several other symptoms all happening together.” I just don’t have that memory in a neat way.

It’s more like scattered impressions—being tired sometimes, being hard on myself sometimes, not feeling very engaged sometimes—but I can’t tell if those were part of one sustained period or just normal stress piling up. And because I didn’t talk to anyone about it or track it at the time, it’s hard to reconstruct now without feeling like I’m guessing.

So the most truthful answer is that I’m not sure. I can’t think of a definite past episode before this one that fits what you’re describing.
